agenda: Welcome and how the cohort works
What AI agents are and what they can do for an executive
Getting set up: accounts and connecting email, calendar and files
Live demo: an assistant working on real tasks
Hands-on: set up your own workspace with help
Wrap-up and first homework
description:
Our Q1 2027 cohort, AI for Business Executives, starts the week of January 11. It is a live, guided program for leaders who do not code but want AI to take real work off their plate.

Each week has one 90-minute live session: a short lesson, a live demo, then hands-on practice with help in the room. Weekly office hours give you time to bring questions and anything that did not work.

Early sessions cover getting set up, building a meeting and note-taker workflow, and an accounting workflow. Later sessions move into assistants and agents built for your own role.

Seats are limited to 30. Join the interest list to save your spot and get the full curriculum when it is released.
prerequisites: No coding experience needed.
summary: The first class of our Q1 2027 cohort, a live, hands-on program where non-coding executives learn to build AI agents for their own work.
takeaways: A working AI setup connected to your email, calendar and files
A clear picture of what you will build over the cohort
Your first small task automated
A plan for which work to hand to AI first
title: Q1 2027 Cohort: AI for Business Executives,

agenda: 1. Walk one piece of content from idea to post
2. Mark each step as craft, which stays human, or mechanics, which a light tool can take
3. Live: a content bank as the single home for ideas
4. Live: /wf-council stress-tests the hand-off plan from five angles
description: Before adding any tool, find out where the time actually goes. The creative work is rarely the slow part. The slow parts are the handoffs, the resizing and the hunting for the latest version. This session walks one piece of content from idea to post and marks each step as craft, which stays human, or mechanics, which a light tool can take. Live: a content bank as the single home for ideas, and /wf-council, which stress-tests the hand-off plan from five angles. Presented by James Christopher.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the terminal and Claude Code. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.
summary: Find the steps that eat your team's week, and decide which ones a light AI tool should take.
takeaways: A pipeline time audit worksheet
A content bank template
title: Where the Hours Go: Mapping Your Content Pipeline

agenda: 1. One idea, every format: a LinkedIn image, an Instagram post, a vertical cover and a short animation
2. Live: /wf-design places your exact copy and your own images into Canva layouts at each platform size
3. Live: /wf-motion turns the same message into a 6 to 10 second animation
4. Check every output and approve every result
description: A single idea has to become a LinkedIn image, an Instagram post, a vertical cover and a short animation. This session shows how to do that without another round in a design tool for each one. Live: /wf-design places your exact copy and your own images into Canva layouts at each platform size and waits for your pick. /wf-motion turns the same message into a 6 to 10 second animation. Every output is checked before you see it, and you approve every result. Presented by James Christopher.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the terminal and Claude Code. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.
summary: Turn one approved idea into every platform format, with your words and images left exactly as you made them.
takeaways: A one-idea, every-format checklist
title: One Idea, Every Format: Production Without the Resizing

agenda: 1. From one long recording to vertical shorts with captions, clean audio and a thumbnail
2. Live: /vid pulls shorts from a long video
3. Live: /wf-design youtube builds thumbnail layouts
4. Choose the moments and check the cuts
description: One good recording can feed a month of posts, if someone has the hours to cut it. This session shows how to get from footage you already have to vertical shorts with captions, clean audio and a thumbnail. Live: /vid pulls shorts from a long video, and /wf-design youtube builds thumbnail layouts. Speaker quotes are used only when the speaker has approved them. You choose the moments. The tools do the cutting. Presented by James Christopher.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the terminal and Claude Code. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.
summary: Get from one long recording to captioned shorts and a thumbnail, without days of editing.
takeaways: A one-recording, many-posts plan
title: Video Without the Editing Bay

agenda: 1. What every platform needs: caption length, hashtags, alt text and YouTube metadata
2. Live: /wf-pack builds a review-ready folder per platform
3. Live: review and post by hand from /desk
4. Scheduling, and why it always asks first
description: A finished post still has to go out to four platforms, each with its own caption length, hashtags, alt text and, for YouTube, a title, description and tags. This session shows how to prepare all of it in one step. Live: /wf-pack builds a review-ready folder per platform, and /desk is where a person reviews and posts by hand. Scheduling is available, but it always asks first. The tools prepare. Your team posts. Presented by James Christopher.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the terminal and Claude Code. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.
summary: Prepare every platform's caption, alt text and metadata at once, and still post each item yourself.
takeaways: A weekly distribution routine for a small team
title: Distribution Without the Copy-Paste

agenda: 1. Where voice slips and claims go unchecked as production speeds up
2. Live: /audit scores a draft for AI tells
3. Live: /human repairs stiff copy, /fact verifies claims with sources, and /hook compares first lines
4. Start your taste charter
description: Once production speeds up, the voice can slip and claims can go out unchecked. This session shows a few quick checks that hold every draft to your own standards. Live: /audit scores a draft for AI tells and sends it back to a person after two failed revisions. /human repairs stiff copy, /fact verifies claims with sources, and /hook compares first lines. Presented by James Christopher.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of the terminal and Claude Code. Codex also works, but Claude Code is preferred.
summary: Keep your voice and your facts intact as production speeds up, without adding an approval committee.
takeaways: A taste charter template
The Zero-Clickbait, Zero-Robot Guide
The four rules as a team policy
title: Keeping It Yours: Light Quality Checks for a Small Team
